lessons.title: Unit 1: At my birthday party – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support listening to and pronouncing English vocabulary through a text-to-speech tool. The teacher lets pupils listen to model pronunciations of the words pasta, pizza, popcorn and identify the word that matches each picture; Health education: Recognise some foods commonly served at parties; build healthy eating habits and avoid wasting food; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 1: At my birthday party – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen to the audio, look at the pictures of pasta / pizza / popcorn and choose or tick the matching picture; Digital competence 4.2.CB1a: Begin to recognise personal information that needs to be protected when using digital devices. The teacher reminds pupils not to post photos, dates of birth, birthday party locations or family information online without permission; Ethics: Share food, wait for their turn and behave politely at birthday parties; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 1: At my birthday party – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and give pronunciation feedback on simple English sentence patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils say “The popcorn is yummy.” / “The pizza is yummy.” / “The pasta is yummy.” and listen to the pronunciation support tool read the model sentences back; Digital competence 2.1.CB1a: Take part in simple digital communication activities in a learning environment guided by the teacher. Pupils listen to the song, look at the pictures and practise the sentence patterns with the class; Culture and communication education: Use positive words when commenting on food and show a cheerful, polite attitude at birthday parties; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 2: In the backyard – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support listening to and pronouncing English vocabulary. The teacher lets pupils listen to model pronunciations of the words kite, bike, kitten; pupils listen, point to the pictures and repeat; Road safety: Teach pupils to wear helmets and ride bicycles in safe areas with adult supervision; Animal care education: Play gently with pets such as kittens, take care of them and do not tease them; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 2: In the backyard – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen to the sentence, look at the two pictures and choose/circle the matching one; AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI tools can create or read model sentences from pictures. The teacher has pupils compare the sentence read by AI with the picture to decide on the correct content; Digital competence 4.1.CB1a: Begin to build habits of using digital devices safely: sit properly, keep a suitable distance from the screen and follow the teacher's instructions; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 2: In the backyard – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking and pronunciation practice of simple question–answer patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils listen to the model Is he/she …? – Yes, he/she is. / No, he/she isn’t. and then practise speaking with the pictures; Digital competence 2.1.CB1a: Take part in simple digital communication activities in a learning environment guided by the teacher: listen to questions, choose pictures and answer in turns; Life skills: Encourage safe outdoor activity, sharing toys and waiting for one's turn when playing with friends; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Fun time 1 – Lesson 1
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: The teacher may use AI voices/images checked in advance to create a fun challenge; pupils compare them with the pictures, words and sentence patterns they have learnt, and do not treat AI output as the default answer; Digital competence 2.4.CB1a: Take part in simple digital games/learning resources in groups; wait for their turn, choose answers and respond politely; Character education: Cooperate, play honestly and respect friends; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Fun time 1 – Lesson 2
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.2.CB1a: Observe, listen to and select simple information on teacher-controlled digital learning resources; check again when an answer does not match the picture/audio; AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can generate voices or suggest answers but is sometimes wrong; pupils need to ask the teacher/check the textbook before correcting their work; Digital safety education: No personal account is needed; do not enter private information; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 3: At the seaside – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support listening to and pronouncing English vocabulary through a text-to-speech tool. The teacher has pupils listen to and identify the words kite, bike, kitten; pupils point to the matching pictures and practise the /k/ sound; Safety education: Remind pupils to wear helmets and play/ride bicycles in safe areas with adult supervision; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 3: At the seaside – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen, look at the pictures and choose/circle the correct answer in the pairs kite – bike and kitten – dog; Digital competence 4.1.CB1a: Begin to build habits of using digital devices safely: sit properly, keep a suitable distance from the screen and only operate the device when the teacher gives instructions; Animal care education: Play gently with pets; do not tease or hurt animals; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 3: At the seaside – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and give pronunciation feedback on simple English sentence patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils listen to the models and practise saying: “Let’s look at the sea!” / “Let’s look at the sail!” / “Let’s look at the sand!”; Digital competence 2.1.CB1a: Take part in simple digital communication activities in a guided learning environment: listen to models, look at the pictures and choose suitable words to complete the sentence “Let’s ____!”; Environmental education: Develop awareness of keeping beaches clean, not littering and protecting natural landscapes; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 4: In the countryside – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support listening to and pronouncing English vocabulary through a text-to-speech tool. The teacher has pupils listen to and identify the words road, river, rainbow; pupils point to the correct pictures and practise the /r/ sound; Road safety: Recognise roads in the countryside; remind pupils to walk on the correct part of the road, look carefully when crossing and wear a helmet when riding on a motorbike/e-bike; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 4: In the countryside – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen to sentences with the key words road / river / rainbow and then choose or circle the matching pictures; Digital competence 4.1.CB1a: Begin to build habits of using digital devices safely: only touch/select as instructed, do not open unfamiliar content on their own and keep a suitable distance from the screen; Environmental protection: Be aware of keeping rivers and village roads clean; do not throw rubbish into rivers or public places; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 4: In the countryside – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and pronunciation checking of simple English sentence patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils practise asking and answering: “What can you see?” – “I can see a rainbow/river/road.” The teacher may use a model-reading tool so that pupils listen, repeat and adjust their own pronunciation; Digital competence 2.1.CB1a: Take part in simple digital communication activities in a guided learning environment: listen to questions, look at the pictures and choose suitable answers; Local education – Environmental education: Recognise the beauty of the rural landscape of the homeland; help keep village roads, rivers and the landscape green, clean and beautiful; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Review 1 – Phil and Sue
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.B1: Recognise that an AI-style answer/illustration may not match the story; pupils check it against the pictures and the textbook content; Digital competence 1.2.CB1a: Find simple information in the story/digital learning resources to confirm answers; Character education: Be honest when stating what they have heard/read

lessons.title: Review 1 – Self – check – Part 1
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Listen, choose and check answers on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance; AI 2.A2: Compare a simple AI suggestion with the answer based on the picture/audio and correct it if it is wrong; Self-study education: Mark the content they have done well and the content that needs more practice

lessons.title: Review 1 – Self – check – Part 2
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 5.2.CB1a: Choose suitable simple tools for revision (audio, digital flashcards, digital games provided by the teacher); AI 2.B1: Do not copy AI answers; pupils do the task themselves first, then use AI examples to check under the teacher's guidance; Honesty education: Complete the Self-check section independently

lessons.title: Unit 5: In the classroom – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support listening to and pronouncing English vocabulary through a text-to-speech tool. The teacher has pupils listen to and identify the words question, square, quiz; pupils point to the correct pictures and practise the initial sound of the letter Q, q; Ethics - classroom routines: Raise their hands to answer, listen to the teacher and classmates, and wait for their turn in class activities; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 5: In the classroom – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen to sentences with the key words square / question / quiz and then choose or mark the matching pictures; Digital competence 4.1.CB1a: Begin to build habits of using digital devices safely: only touch/select as instructed, do not open unfamiliar content on their own and keep a suitable distance from the screen; Health protection: Sit properly, keep a suitable distance when looking at the screen/board and rest their eyes after digital activities; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 5: In the classroom – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and pronunciation checking of simple English sentence patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils practise asking and answering: “What’s she doing?” - “She’s colouring a square.”; “What’s he doing?” - “He’s doing a quiz.” The teacher may use a model-reading tool so that pupils listen, repeat and adjust their own pronunciation; Digital competence 2.1.CB1a: Take part in simple digital communication activities in a guided learning environment: listen to questions, look at the pictures and choose/say suitable answers; Ethics: Develop honesty when doing quizzes, do not look at classmates' work and encourage friends in learning activities; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.theme: Me and the world around me
lessons.title: Unit 6: On the farm – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)

lessons.theme: Me and the world around me
lessons.title: Unit 6: On the farm – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. lessons.theme: Me and the world around me
lessons.title: Unit 6: On the farm – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)

lessons.title: Fun time 2 – Lesson 1

lessons.title: Fun time 2 – Lesson 2
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.2.CB1a: Observe, listen to and select simple information on teacher-controlled digital learning resources; check again when an answer does not match the picture/audio; AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can generate voices or suggest answers but is sometimes wrong; pupils need to ask the teacher/check the textbook before correcting their work; Digital safety education: No personal account is needed; do not enter private information; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 7: In the kitchen – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support listening to and pronouncing English vocabulary through a text-to-speech tool. The teacher has pupils listen to, identify and point to the correct pictures for the words juice, jelly, jam; pupils practise the letter J, j and the /dʒ/ sound; Health education: Recognise some familiar foods and drinks; begin to build healthy eating habits and choose suitable food; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 7: In the kitchen – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen to the sentences “I like jam/juice/jelly.” and then choose or tick the matching pictures; look at the letters and complete the missing words; Digital competence 4.1.CB1a: Begin to build habits of using digital devices safely and for the right purpose: only open learning resources provided by the teacher; do not click on advertisements or unfamiliar links on their own; Thrift education - avoiding waste: Take just enough food and drink and do not leave leftovers; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 7: In the kitchen – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and pronunciation checking of simple English communication patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils practise the pattern “Pass me the jam, please.” - “Here you are.” and substitute juice/jelly. The teacher may use a model-reading tool so that pupils listen, repeat and adjust their own pronunciation; Digital competence 2.1.CB1a: Take part in simple guided digital communication activities: listen to requests, look at the pictures and choose/say suitable responses; Ethics - communication skills: Use the word “please”, say thank you and pass things to others politely at mealtimes; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 8: In the village – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support listening to and pronouncing English vocabulary through a text-to-speech tool. The teacher has pupils listen to, identify and point to the correct pictures for the words village, van, volleyball; pupils practise the letter V, v and the /v/ sound; Local education: Recognise some familiar images of the countryside; develop love for and awareness of preserving the landscape where they live; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 8: In the village – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen to the sentences “This is a van/village/volleyball.” and then choose or circle the matching pictures; look at the pictures and complete the missing words; Digital competence 4.1.CB1a: Begin to build habits of using digital devices for the right purpose: only work on learning resources opened by the teacher and stop using the device when asked; Road safety: Recognise that a van is a means of transport; sit properly, fasten the seat belt if there is one and do not play around in the vehicle; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 8: In the village – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and pronunciation checking of simple English communication patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils practise the pattern “Can you draw a van?” - “Yes, I can.” / “No, I can’t.” and substitute volleyball, football, village. lessons.title: Reserve period 1
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 2.4.CB1a: Take part in simple digital activities organised by the teacher where appropriate; AI 2.A1: Recall the principle that AI only supports; information must be checked before it is used; Flexible education: Content is adjusted to the actual situation

lessons.title: Unit 9: In the grocery store – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)

The teacher has pupils listen to, identify and point to the correct pictures for the words yogurt, yams, yo-yos; pupils practise the letter Y, y and the /j/ sound; Health education: Choose suitable food, eat sensibly and do not eat any food without an adult's permission; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 9: In the grocery store – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and pronunciation checking of simple English communication patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils practise the pattern “What do you want?” - “I want some yams.” and substitute yogurt, yo-yos; Life skills/Ethics: Speak politely when buying or receiving things; queue, take just enough and be thrifty to avoid waste; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 13: In the maths class – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and pronunciation checking of question - answer patterns about numbers. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils practise: “What number is it?” - “It’s eleven/twelve/thirteen/fourteen/fifteen.”; Digital competence 2.1.CB1a: Take part in simple digital communication activities in a guided learning environment: listen to models, look at the number cards and say the number shown correctly; Learning skills: Develop quick reactions in recognising numbers, answer confidently and wait for their turn in question - answer games; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 14: At home – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support listening to, identifying and pronouncing English vocabulary about family members. The teacher has pupils listen to and identify the words sister, brother, grandmother; pupils match the words with the pictures and practise the letter cluster er; Family education: Love, respect and care for brothers, sisters and grandparents in the family; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 14: At home – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen, look at the pictures and choose the correct character/age in the Listen and circle activity; then complete Write and say with grandmother, brother, sister; Maths integration: Consolidate recognising and reading ages up to 20, especially the numbers 16, 17, 18, 19, 20; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 14: At home – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support speaking practice and pronunciation checking of question - answer patterns about age. Pupils practise “How old is your brother?” - “He’s nineteen.” and substitute suitable ages; Digital competence 4.2.CB1a: Recognise that the ages and pictures of family members are personal information that must be used carefully in the digital environment. Do not share them without an adult's permission; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Fun time 4 – Lesson 1
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: The teacher may use AI voices/images checked in advance to create a fun challenge; pupils compare them with the pictures, words and sentence patterns they have learnt, and do not treat AI output as the default answer; Digital competence 2.4.CB1a: Take part in simple digital games/learning resources in groups; wait for their turn, choose answers and respond politely; Character education: Cooperate, play honestly and respect friends; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Fun time 4 – Lesson 2
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.2.CB1a: Observe, listen to and select simple information on teacher-controlled digital learning resources; check again when an answer does not match the picture/audio; AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can generate voices or suggest answers but is sometimes wrong; pupils need to ask the teacher/check the textbook before correcting their work; Digital safety education: No personal account is needed; do not enter private information; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 15: In the clothes shop – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support image recognition and pronunciation of English vocabulary about clothes. The teacher has pupils look at the pictures and listen to the tool read the words shoes, shirts, shorts; pupils point to the correct items and practise the /ʃ/ sound in the letter cluster sh; Life skills: Keep clothes and shoes clean and tidy, and choose clothes suitable for the activity and the weather; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 15: In the clothes shop – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen, look and choose the correct pictures in the Listen and tick activity; then complete Write and say with the words shirts, shoes, shorts; Digital competence 4.1.CB1a: Begin to recognise how to use digital devices safely when viewing shopping pictures or learning resources: only operate as instructed; do not click on advertisements or unfamiliar links on their own; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 15: In the clothes shop – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support listening and speaking practice in situations asking where things are. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils practise the pattern “Where are the shoes?” - “Over there.” and substitute shirts / shorts; Digital competence 4.2.CB1a: Recognise that they must not give their name, address, phone number or payment information on their own when viewing shopping content on digital devices; ask an adult when asked to enter information; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 16: At the campsite – Lesson 1 (Activities 1–2)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A1: Recognise that AI can support image recognition and pronunciation of English vocabulary. The teacher has pupils look at camping pictures, listen to a model-reading tool and identify the words tent, teapot, blanket; pupils practise the initial /t/ sound in tent, teapot; Life skills: Recognise some items needed for camping and arrange them neatly in the right places; Safety: Do not go near barbecue grills, boiling water or fire on their own without an adult; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 16: At the campsite – Lesson 2 (Activities 3–5)
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Perform simple information-selection actions on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance. Pupils listen and choose/circle the pictures matching the words and positions in the lesson: tent, blanket, teapot; near, in, on; Digital competence 4.1.CB1a: Follow the rules for using digital devices safely: only touch/select as instructed; do not open other apps or links on their own; Environmental protection: Keep the campsite clean, collect rubbish and do not damage trees, flowers and grass; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Unit 16: At the campsite – Lesson 3 (Activities 6–8)
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.A2: Recognise that AI can support listening and speaking practice and give pronunciation feedback on simple English sentence patterns. Under the teacher's guidance, pupils practise asking and answering: “Is the blanket near the tent?” - “No, it isn’t. It’s in the tent.”; substitute table, teapot, tent; Digital competence 2.1.CB1a: Take part in simple digital communication activities in a guided learning environment: listen to models, look at the pictures and choose suitable answers; Camping safety education: Stay close to adults, do not leave the camping area on their own and follow the safety instructions; Life skills: Communication skills: confidently greet others and introduce themselves in simple sentences

lessons.title: Review 4 – Phil and Sue
lessons.adjustments: AI 2.B1: Recognise that an AI-style answer/illustration may not match the story; pupils check it against the pictures and the textbook content; Digital competence 1.2.CB1a: Find simple information in the story/digital learning resources to confirm answers; Character education: Be honest when stating what they have heard/read

lessons.title: Review 4 – Self – check – Part 1
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 1.1.CB1a: Listen, choose and check answers on digital learning resources under the teacher's guidance; AI 2.A2: Compare a simple AI suggestion with the answer based on the picture/audio and correct it if it is wrong; Self-study education: Mark the content they have done well and the content that needs more practice

lessons.title: Review 4 – Self – check – Part 2
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 5.2.CB1a: Choose suitable simple tools for revision (audio, digital flashcards, digital games provided by the teacher); AI 2.B1: Do not copy AI answers; pupils do the task themselves first, then use AI examples to check under the teacher's guidance; Honesty education: Complete the Self-check section independently

lessons.title: Reserve period 2
lessons.adjustments: Digital competence 2.4.CB1a: Take part in simple digital activities organised by the teacher where appropriate; AI 2.A1: Recall the principle that AI only supports; information must be checked before it is used; Flexible education: Content is adjusted to the actual situation
